activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Lillian wanted to build a house for her toy snake. She looked for walls in her block box. First she tried the round blocks. They rolled away! Round blocks cannot be walls, she thought.

Then she found square blocks. She stacked them up. Four flat sides, side by side. The wall stood tall! "Look, snake, a square wall!" she said. She made a long wall with rectangle blocks, too. The rectangles were like big long squares.

Now she needed a roof. Squares were too flat. Then she saw a triangle block. It had three sides and a pointy top. She set it on the wall. It sat just right! "A triangle roof!" she shouted.

She put her snake inside. "Welcome home, silly snake," she said. The snake peeked out the round window she had left. Then Lillian grabbed crayons to color a flag for the top. A square flag, of course.

activity: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
knowledge_domain: getting a vaccination shot at the doctor's office
story:
Owen sat in the waiting room with his mom. He wanted to feel brave. But today he would get a shot. He held his stuffed bear, Brown Bear, very tight.

"Will the shot hurt?" Owen asked.

"Just a tiny pinch," said Mom. "Then it is done."

A nurse stepped in. "Hello, Owen," she said. "Do you want your bear to get a shot first?" Owen looked at Brown Bear. The nurse touched the bear's arm with a cotton ball. "All done," she said. "Brown Bear was so still."

Then it was Owen's turn. He sat on Mom's lap. She gave him a nice, big hug. The nurse cleaned his arm. Then came the tiny pinch. Owen blinked. It was over already!

"Why did the bear go first?" Owen asked.

"Because the bear showed you it was quick," said Mom.

Owen looked at his arm. There was a small bandage with a star on it. "My turn is done," he said. He held Brown Bear up high. "We are both brave."

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Lena woke up in her bedroom. She ran to the window. "Is it store day now?" she asked. Yesterday Grandma had said, "We will go to the store in two days." But how many days had gone by?

Lena looked at her little calendar. Every night, Grandma put one sticker on it. Yesterday had a sun sticker. Yesterday was gone, like a finished bowl of cereal. Today had no sticker yet. So the store was not today. It was tomorrow.

"Can tomorrow hurry up?" Lena asked. Grandma smiled. "Tomorrow comes after we sleep," she said. "First we eat, then we play, then night comes."

Later that day, thunder made a loud boom. Rain tapped the window. Lena watched the drops. The rain came, and then puddles came. One thing made another thing happen, just like that.

That night, Grandma helped Lena pick a star sticker. Lena pressed it onto today. Now today was finished too. "Thank you, star," she whispered. She closed her eyes.

In the morning, the sun was bright. Lena jumped up. She looked at the calendar. There was one empty square left. "That square is today!" she shouted. Today was store day at last. She ran to find her shoes.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Athena ran to the park with Dad. The sun was out. It was a sunny day. Athena wore her sun hat. Then the wind came. It blew her hat right off!

"My hat flew away!" said Athena. The windy day took the hat under a tree. Dad got it back. "Hold it tight," said Dad. Athena held it tight.

Then gray clouds grew big and dark. Rain fell. Plop, plop, plop. Athena was scared of getting wet. "Don't worry," said Dad. He gave her a rain coat and rain boots. Now the rain could not get her. Athena jumped in a brown puddle. Splash! Her boots kept her feet dry.

Later it got very cold. Soft white snow began to fall. "Look, snow!" said Athena. Dad put warm mittens on her hands. She caught a snowflake in her mitten. Then she and Dad drank warm cocoa from a little glass cup. "Sunny, rainy, windy, snowy," said Athena. Dad smiled and held her hand.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Aubrey sat at the dinner table. She had green beans on her plate. She did not want them.

"I want to count them," said Aubrey.

Mama smiled. "Count with me."

Aubrey poked one bean. "One." She poked another. "Two, three, four." The beans rolled apart. "Five, six, seven." More rolling. "Eight, nine, ten!" Ten beans, all counted.

Dada peeked over his cup. "Ten beans! That is a lot."

Aubrey looked at her beans. Then she ate one. "Now there are nine," she said. She ate another one. "Eight!" She ate one more. "Seven, six, five."

Dada laughed. "Each bite makes the pile smaller."

Aubrey kept going. "Four, three, two." One bean left. Little brother Ben looked upset. He had no beans yet. His plate was empty.

"Here, Ben," said Aubrey. She gave him her last bean. "One bean for you."

Ben clapped his hands. He made a happy sound.

"Zero beans for me," said Aubrey. "All done!"

Mama gave her a small spoonful of rice. Aubrey peeked at it. "One spoon," she said. "Maybe I can count that too."

Dada poured milk into her cup. The milk went up and up. "Stop!" said Aubrey, laughing. "It will make a river!"

Mama stopped just in time. "No milk river tonight," she said.

Aubrey drank her milk. Then she counted her spoons of rice. "One, two, three, all gone."

Ben banged his spoon on his tray. "More!" he said.

"Ben wants to count too," said Aubrey.

Mama put three peas on Ben's tray. Ben pushed them around with his spoon. "Ba, ba, ba," he said.

"He is trying," said Aubrey. "Good job, Ben."

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
story:
Charlie sat in her reading nook with her letter cards. Mama sat close by with a cup of tea. Charlie held up the card with B on it. "B says buh," she said. She looked around the nook. Her bear sat on the pillow. She put the B card next to the bear. The bear got a letter!

She held up the card with F on it. "F says fff," she said. A soft feather lay by her blanket. She put the F card on the feather. The feather got a letter too!

Then she held up S. She could not remember the sound. Her tummy felt tight. "I forgot this one," she said. Mama gave her hand a little pat. Charlie wiggled her toes. Her socks were stinky! She laughed. "S says sss, like stinky socks!" She put the S card on her sock.

Then she poured pretend tea for bear, feather, and socks. "Tea for all my letters!" said Charlie.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Ava and her family drove to the beach. Grandma came too. Ava held her small yellow bucket the whole way. "Is this Grandma's beach?" Ava asked. "Yes, it is," said Grandma.

Ava wanted to find a shell. She looked and looked. Then she saw one by the water. The waves came in. The water lifted the shell. The shell floated up and slid back to Ava's feet. She picked it up. "The water brought it to me!" she said.

Grandma held Ava's hand. They walked a short way along the sand. Ava put the shell in her bucket. The sun felt warm. "Time for a snack," said Grandma. They sat together on a big towel. Ava ate her crackers and smiled. "We can come back tomorrow," said Grandma. Ava hugged her shell tight.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Ivy went to the library with Dad. She got her very own card. It had her name on it. She picked a book about a worm in a garden. "I want to keep this book forever," she said.

Dad shook his head. "Not forever," he said. "Other kids want to read it too. We bring it back soon." Ivy held the book tight. The book smelled like paper. The pages felt dry and smooth.

At home, Ivy read the worm book three times. Then she read it again. After some days, Dad said, "Time to take the book back." Ivy was sad. But then she saw the shelf of books. So many books! She could take a new one home. Ivy put the worm book in her bag. "I will borrow another one," she said.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Raphael stood in the pool changing room. He held his new goggles in his hands. They looked big and round like frog eyes. "Will they stay on?" he asked. "Let's try," said Dad.

Dad helped him pull the straps tight. Raphael blinked. The world looked blue and clear. Then he put them on his head. The straps snapped back and hit his nose. "Ouch," said Raphael. But then he laughed too. He tried again, slow and careful. This time the goggles sat just right.

In the pool, Raphael put his face in the water. He could see his toes. He could see Dad's legs. He could even see a shiny coin on the bottom. "Look, Dad!" he said. Dad smiled and held his hand. "Ready to kick?" asked Dad. Raphael kicked and the water went splash.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
story:
Sofia sat at the big table. She had her letter cards in a small bag. She pulled them out one by one.

" That is M," she said. "Mmm, mmm." Her mouth made the sound all by itself. She tried B. "Buh, buh." Her lips popped open when she said it. She tried S. "Ssss." Her mouth made a long thin sound, like a snake.

Then Sofia tried P. "Puh." A little bit of air came out. She held her hand in front of her lips. She said "Puh" again. She felt the air puff on her fingers! She stopped and stared at her hand.

"Mmm," she said. No air puff. "Buh." A tiny puff. "Puh." A big puff. She tried each card again. Some letters pushed air at her hand. Some letters did not.

Sofia ran to find her big brother, Marco. He was so young when he learned these cards, Mom said. "Marco, put your hand here," Sofia said. She held up the P card. "Puh!"

Marco felt the puff. "Do it again," he said. Sofia smiled and said, "Puh, puh, puh."

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Aaron went to the pool with his dad. He was learning to swim. Aaron was scared of the huge pool. "Will the water hold me up?" he asked. "Yes," said Dad. "You will wear your water wings."

Aaron held Dad's hand. He stepped in. He kicked his legs. He blew bubbles. Dad held him the whole time.

Then it was time to get out. They went to the changing room. Aaron was shaking. His teeth went click, click. "Why am I cold?" he asked. "Your skin is all wet," said Dad. Dad wrapped Aaron in a big towel.

Aaron sat still. His skin got warm. His teeth stopped clicking. "The towel made me warm," said Aaron.

Then something fell on the floor. It was Aaron's goggles. They left a drip of water. The drip made a little blue spot, like paint. Aaron laughed. "My goggles are painting the floor," he said.

Dad laughed too. He helped Aaron get dressed. Aaron put on his warm socks. "Next time I will blow more bubbles," said Aaron. Dad gave him a hug.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Liam looked out the big window. The sun was bright. "It is sunny today," said Mom. Liam put on his little cap. Off went the cap, because the sun made him too warm.

Then the sky turned gray. Rain fell, tap tap tap. Liam heard it on the roof. He looked for his rain boots. Mom helped him put them on. Liam and Mom stepped outside. The rain made little puddles on the stones. Liam jumped in one. Splash! His boots kept his feet dry.

The wind came next. It blew the tree back and forth. Liam's scarf flapped like a wing. "Where is the wind going?" Liam asked. Mom said, "The wind goes where it wants to." Then soft white snow began to fall. Liam held out his mitten. A snowflake sat on it. Mom zipped his coat up straight. "Warm now," said Liam. He caught one more snowflake on his tongue.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Sara found a big orange scarf on the bench. She picked it up. She held it over two chairs. It made a roof. Now she had a little house!

"I need a baby," said Sara. She put her teddy bear in the house. The wind blew. The roof fell down. The teddy fell over too. "Oh no," said Sara.

She looked around. She found a stick. She pushed the stick under the scarf. The stick held the roof up. The wind blew again. This time the roof stayed!

"One chair, two chairs, one stick, one teddy," said Sara. "My house is strong now."

She gave teddy a pretend bottle. He drank it all up. Then teddy got a hug.

Sara heard her mom call, "Time to go home!" Sara waved at the little house. "See you later, house!" she said. She took teddy's paw and walked to the gate.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Emilia wants a book about sleepy bears. She and Mama go to the library. There are so many books!

Emilia finds a red book. She opens it. The pages have little marks on them. "Those are words," Mama says. "The words tell the story." Emilia turns the pages. First this page, then that page, all the way to the end.

"Can I keep it forever?" Emilia asks.

"We take it home," says the librarian. "Then we bring it back on library day. Other kids want to read it too."

Emilia hugs the book. At home, Mama reads it to her. Emilia kicks her feet on the floor. One story, two stories, three stories, again!

On library day, Emilia holds the red book. She gives it back to the librarian.

"Good returning," says the librarian. "Now it is someone else's turn."

Emilia picks out a new book. It is blue. She opens it and looks at the words. "Read this one too, Mama," she says.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Amelia ran to the play corner at daycare. She wanted to play house with her friend Ben. But Ben already had the baby doll. He hugged it tight.

Amelia peeked in the little toy crib. It was empty. Then she saw the teddy bear under the chair. "You can be my baby," she told the teddy. She wrapped it in a small blanket. She held it in her arm and rocked it side to side.

The teddy's eyes fell shut? No, but Amelia made a soft snore sound. "Shh, baby is sleeping," she said. Ben put his doll down too. He ran to get a toy pot. "I will cook soup," he said. Their teacher, Miss Kim, stirred the pretend pot with a big wooden spoon. "Almost ready," said Miss Kim.

Amelia's teddy woke up with a wide yawn. She held it close. "Time to eat, baby," she said. She tapped the teddy's mouth with a toy spoon. "Yum, yum!" said Ben, and he clapped his hands.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Clara wants to help at school. Teacher Max is making warm soup for snack time. He stirs the big pot. Clara has a small cup of cold water. She puts her fingers near the pot. "Hot," says Teacher Max. "Stay back, please." Clara steps away.

Clara wants to help fast. She runs to get a spoon. The spoon falls on the floor. "Slow down," says Teacher Max with a smile. Clara walks back, slow and careful. She picks up the spoon. Now she can stir the little bowl of fruit. She stirs slow, slow, slow.

Then Clara sees something. Her cold cup sits in the sun by the window. She touches it. The cup feels warm now! The sun made cold water turn warm. "Teacher Max, come look!" He puts his hand on the cup. "You found it," he says. "That is a good trick."

Sam from the rug calls, "Was it a joke? Did you hide the warmth?" Clara laughs. "No, the sun is a little naughty. It took my cold away." Sam laughs too. Teacher Max gives Clara a broom. Clara helps sweep the crumbs under the table, big sweeps and small sweeps. She sweeps up one crumb that hides by the chair leg. "I see you," she tells it, and sweeps it into the dustpan.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Lucy wanted to paint a picture for her doll. But she could not find the paint cups. "Where did they go?" she asked. She looked under the table. She looked in the toy box. Then she looked in the deep toy basket. There they were!

Lucy set out four cups. Red, blue, yellow, green. "One, two, three, four," she said. She tapped her brush. She put red paint on the paper. Then she put yellow paint right on top. Something funny happened. The red and yellow spot turned orange!

"Ooh," said Lucy. "Red and yellow make orange!" She tried blue and yellow next. That spot turned green like grass. Then she dipped red into blue. That spot turned purple like grapes.

Her doll sat on the chair and watched. "Which color do you like best?" Lucy asked her. The doll did not say. Lucy laughed. "I think you like all of them."

Mama came to look. "What a pretty picture," said Mama. Lucy held it up high. "Look, doll! Red, blue, yellow, green, and orange, green, purple too!"

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Logan had a little drum. He wanted to play a song for Mom. He hit the drum with his hand. It made a big boom. Logan hit it soft. It made a tiny tap.

"What a small sound," said Mom.

Logan wanted a big song. He hit hard, but not too hard. The drum went boom, boom, boom. Then Logan stopped. He wanted the drum to be quiet. He held his hand still on top. The drum stopped right away.

"You made it quiet all by yourself," said Mom.

The cat ran into the room. Logan tapped soft, soft, soft. The cat sat down to listen. It did not run away. Logan tapped a little louder. The cat's ears went up.

"A song for the cat," said Logan.

Mom clapped her hands. Logan read the drum like a book, his hands telling it what to say. He played boom, tap, boom. The cat purred on the rug, and Mom sang along.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Aurora is going to the dentist. It is her first time. She holds Mama's hand tight.

The chair is big. It has a wheel on one side. The dentist turns the wheel. The chair goes up, up, up! Aurora laughs. "Can it go down too?" she asks. "Yes," says the dentist. He turns the wheel back. The chair goes down, down, down.

Aurora opens her mouth wide. The dentist counts her teeth. "Ten little teeth," he says. "Open like a hippo!" Aurora opens bigger. The dentist giggles. Then he gives her a small mirror. Aurora looks inside. "I see my teeth!" she says. She turns the mirror a little. Now she sees her own eye. "Silly mirror," she says, and everyone laughs.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story: Isabella ran to the window at school. Yesterday, her class planted little seeds in pots. Today, the pots sat in the sun. But nothing was growing yet. "Where is my plant?" she asked. Miss Kim smiled. "Not now. Water it now, and look again later." Isabella got the small watering can. She tipped it over her pot. The dirt turned dark and wet. She waited. She looked and looked. Still nothing. Miss Kim said, "Come back tomorrow." Tomorrow felt far away. Isabella watered her seed again after dinner time, when the class had a snack. Then she went home to eat dinner with her family. The next day, she ran to the window. A tiny green sprout stood there, high as her finger tip. "You grew!" said Isabella. Miss Kim clapped. "Water it today, and tomorrow it will grow even more." Isabella held her can up high. "I will water you now!"

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Leon was at Grandma's house. It was a snowy day. Leon wanted to bake bread for his family.

"Can we make bread?" Leon asked.

"Yes," said Grandma. "We can make a small loaf."

Grandma let Leon pour the flour. Leon mixed it with a spoon. Then Grandma added warm water. She put in the yeast. Grandma always touched the hot stove, never Leon.

The dough sat in a big bowl. Leon looked at it. The dough was small and flat.

"Why is it so little?" Leon asked.

"Wait and see," said Grandma.

They waited. They washed the bowls. Then Leon looked again. The dough was big and puffy! It had grown and grown.

"It got big!" said Leon.

"The warm water made it rise," said Grandma. She smiled.

Grandma shaped the dough. She put it in the oven. Soon a yummy smell filled the kitchen. The oven made a soft noise.

The bread came out golden. Grandma cut it. Leon carried the plates to the table. Mom and Dad clapped for Leon.

"Try it!" said Leon.

His dad took a big bite. "This is the best bread," he said.

Leon took a bite too. It was warm and good. Outside the snow fell. Inside, Leon felt cozy and happy.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Gabriel went to the park with his dad. The duck pond was quiet. A little fish jumped up and went splash. Gabriel laughed at the silly splash.

Dad brought a hoop and a beanbag. "Throw it in," said Dad. Gabriel threw the beanbag. It went up. Then it came down. It landed on the grass, not in the hoop. Gabriel tried again. He threw it high. The beanbag went up, and then it went down into the hoop. It stayed there. Gabriel clapped his hands. "It fell right in!"

Then Dad rolled a big ball to him. The ball was too big for one hand. It bumped his arm and rolled away. Gabriel held out both hands. Dad rolled the ball again. Gabriel caught it with two hands. The ball sat still in his arms like a warm, round pumpkin.

They sat on the bench by the café window. Gabriel looked at the fish pond through the glass. The little fish jumped again. Splash. "Did you see that?" said Gabriel. Dad smiled and rolled the big ball one more time. Gabriel caught it with both hands.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Wyatt wanted to help set the table. Mom said, "We need ten crackers." Wyatt started to count them out. "One, two, three," he said. The crackers made a crunchy sound in the bowl.

He put a small cracker on his sister's plate. She smiled and clapped. "Four, five, six," he counted. Then a tiny crumb fell on the floor. A small bug came out to look at it. Wyatt laughed. "Hello, bug," he said. Mom swept the crumb away. The bug went home too.

"Seven, eight, nine," said Wyatt. He looked in the bowl. Only one cracker was left. "Ten!" he said. He put it on the last plate. The table was ready. Wyatt sang his counting song. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" Dad came in and said, "Perfect. Now we can eat."

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Elizabeth wanted to feed her toy animals. But all her things were mixed up. The toys were with the bananas. The animals were with the crackers. "Oh no," said Elizabeth.

Mama came to help. "Let's make piles," said Mama. Elizabeth put the dog and the cat in one pile. They were animals. She put the ball and the blocks in another pile. They were toys. She put the apple and the bread in the last pile. They were foods.

Then Elizabeth had a big idea. "The animals want food too," she said. She took a toy carrot from the food pile. She gave it to the toy bunny. The bunny got the carrot. Elizabeth clapped her hands. It worked!

Then Elizabeth heard a soft sound outside. She looked out at the street. A real cat sat there. It looked gentle and small. Elizabeth gave the window a kiss. "Bye bye, cat," she said. She waved and waved. The cat stretched in the sun.

"Now my toys are all in piles," said Elizabeth. She hugged the toy bunny tight.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Alexander sat on the small red chair. In front of him was a big drum. His teacher, Miss Rao, handed him two soft sticks.

"Tap the drum," she said. "See what happens."

Alexander lifted a stick. He tapped once. The drum made a deep sound. The skin on top went wobble, wobble. A toy pig sat on the table near the drum. When Alexander tapped hard, the pig bounced a little. When he tapped soft, the pig sat still.

"I can make it jump," said Alexander.

"Try tapping fast," said Miss Rao.

Alexander tapped fast. The pig wiggled and slid toward the edge. Miss Rao caught it with her hand. Alexander laughed and tapped slow this time. The pig did not move at all.

"My sweater feels itchy," said Alexander. He pulled his sleeves down over his hands. Then he tapped the drum with his covered fingers. The sound came out soft, like a whisper.

Miss Rao smiled. "That was a quiet tap," she said.

Alexander tapped soft, then loud, then soft again. The pig sat still, then hopped, then sat still. Alexander tapped his very best slow beat, and the pig stayed calm as a sleeping cat.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Jake stood by the back door. He wanted to play the senses game, but he forgot the words. "Can you help me, Mama?" he asked. "Yes," said Mama. "We can find each one."

Mama picked a red flower. Jake put his nose close. He sniffed. "I smell it with my nose!" he said. "That is one," said Mama. Then they heard a bird sing. Jake pointed to his ears. "I hear it with my ears!" Mama touched the warm dirt. Jake touched it too. "I feel it with my hands!"

The sun felt nice on Jake's face. He closed his eyes. "I feel the sun with my skin!" he said. Then he licked his lips after a sweet berry snack. "I taste with my tongue!" One sense was left. Jake looked all around. He saw a big yellow butterfly. "I see it with my eyes!" he said. "Five senses, all found!" Jake clapped. "I did it!"

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Matthew went to the store with Mama. He wanted apples for a snack. But how many apples should they get?

Mama held up one finger. "Can you count them?" she asked. Matthew put one apple in the bag. "One," he said. He put in another. "Two." He kept going. "Three, four, five."

A lady nearby was counting oranges. "One, two, three, four," she said. Matthew listened. Counting words were everywhere! "Mama, do other people count too?" he asked. "Yes," said Mama. "We count to know how many."

Matthew saw a lamp on a shelf. He touched the shade. It was not hot. It was just warm. "Does the lamp make light?" he asked. Mama nodded. "Press the little button." Matthew pressed it. The lamp made light. He pressed it again. The light went off. "It works!" said Matthew.

At the bread shelf, they counted together. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten," said Matthew. Ten rolls went in the bag. At home, he would eat one apple. Nine would be left. Matthew patted the full bag. "One, two, three," he said, all the way to the door.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Aurora sat on the big clean rug. Family and friends filled the room. Grandma stirred a bowl of dip. Dad opened a bag of chips. On the TV, the big game was starting.

The red team ran with the ball. Aurora picked up her red scarf. She waved it high. Everyone saw her scarf. They waved their arms too. The room filled with cheering.

Then the blue team got the ball. Aurora put her scarf down. She picked up her blue hat. She waved the hat instead. Uncle Ben laughed and waved his blue cup. Everyone cheered for blue now.

The blue team kicked the ball into the net. The whole room jumped up. Aurora jumped too. Grandma handed her a chip with dip. Aurora ate it and waved her hat again. "More blue!" she shouted.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
story:
Elijah wanted to spell his name. He had a big plate of letters. Each letter was a magnet. They lived on the fridge door.

He picked up a letter. "B," said Mama. "B says buh." Elijah put it down. His name did not start with buh. He picked up a wiggly letter. "M," said Mama. "M says mmm." That was not his sound either. Elijah looked and looked. His fingers were sticky from the honey on his toast. One magnet stuck to his thumb. It tickled a little when he pulled it off.

The sticky magnet was E. "E says eh," said Mama. "Eh, eh, Elijah!" Elijah clapped his hands. He put the E on the fridge. Then he found an L. "L says lll," said Mama. Lll was in his name too. Elijah found an I and a J and an A and an H. He lined them all up in a row.

Mama traced the letters with one finger. "E L I J A H," she read. Elijah tapped each letter too. "Eh, lll, ih, juh, ah, huh," he said. The letters made his name. They made sounds when he tapped them. His name was right there on the fridge, made of letters.

Papa came in with his tool box. He had been fixing the gate. Elijah pulled him to the fridge. "Look, Papa! My letters! Tap them!" Papa tapped the E. "Eh," said Elijah. Papa tapped the L. "Lll," said Elijah. Papa tapped every letter, and Elijah said every sound, all the way to the end of his name.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Ellie went to the library with Dad. She wanted to find a book about animals. But she did not know where the animal books were.

The library was big. Ellie saw many shelves. "Let's look," said Dad. Ellie looked at a shelf. She saw trucks and balls and teddy bears. "Toys, toys, toys," said Ellie. Those were toy books, not animal books.

They walked to a new shelf. Ellie saw apples and bread and milk. "Foods, foods, foods," said Ellie. Still no animals. Ellie got a little sad. Dad said, "Try one more shelf."

Ellie tried the next shelf. She saw cats and dogs and ducks. "Animals, animals, animals!" said Ellie. She found the animal books! Ellie picked a big cat book. Then she found a soft pillow in the reading corner. She sat on it with Dad.

Ellie read the cat book. The cat in the book was sleepy. It curled up and went to sleep. Ellie yawned too. "Sleepy girl," said Dad with a smile. He helped Ellie close the book. "Good night, cat," said Ellie.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Ella sat on her bed with her library book. It was a book about a little red cat. She wanted to keep it forever.

She opened the front cover. The first page said "1". The last page said "20". She turned the pages one by one. The words on each page told about the cat. Ella could not read them yet. But her mom could. Mom read them out loud, and the cat story came alive.

"Can the cat be mine?" Ella asked.

"No, it is a library book," said Mom. "We take it back on Thursday. Then another kid can read it too."

Eella held the book tight. She brushed her hand over the smooth cover. Then she looked out at the cloudy sky and thought.

"Can we read it again first?" she asked.

"Yes," said Mom. "We can read it many times before Thursday."

So they read it two more times. Ella turned each page, front to back, all the way to the end. The little red cat went home to his mom. Then Ella put the book on her shelf, next to her paint set.

"Good night, cat," she said. "I will take you back on Thursday."

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story:
Maeva went to the lantern festival with Mama and Papa. The street was full of people. Paper lanterns hung on long strings above them. Maeva wanted to let one go up into the sky, like the big kids did.

Papa held a small lantern for her. "How does it go up?" Maeva asked. "The warm air inside lifts it," Papa said. "It rises slow, like a balloon." Mama lit the candle with a match. Maeva watched from far away, holding Papa's hand.

Then Maeva saw it. The candle made the lantern grow round and fat. The paper puffed out. The lantern pulled up, up, up. "It wants to fly!" she said. Papa let go of the string. The lantern slipped out of his fingers and floated over the rooftops. Maeva waved until it was just a tiny dot. "Goodbye, lantern," she called. "Fly slow."

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Luka ran to the park with his dad. He wanted to play the sense game. His big sister had shown him. Now he wanted to try it all by himself.

Luka closed his eyes. "I hear a bird," he said. "My ears hear it!" Then he touched the slide. "The slide is cold. My hands feel it!" A dog barked. Luka giggled. His ears heard that too.

Then Luka saw something tiny in the grass. It was a shiny red ladybug. Luka got close. "My eyes see it!" he said. His dad handed him an apple. Luka took a bite. He chewed slowly. "My mouth tastes it. Sweet!" Then he sniffed the air. Flowers were growing near the fence. "My nose smells them. They smell like rain!"

Luka stood up tall. "Ears, hands, eyes, mouth, nose," he said. "That is all five!" His dad clapped. "You did it, Luka." Luka spun around fast. "Daddy, watch me!" he shouted. The ladybug flew up. Luka's eyes followed it all the way to the rainbow flowers by the gate.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Athena went to the park with her dad. She wanted to feed the ducks. She had a bag of bread in her hand. "The ducks will like this," she said.

Athena tore off a small piece. She dropped it in the pond. It did not sink. The bread could float! A duck swam over fast. The duck ate the bread. Then more ducks came. They ate the bread too.

But a squirrel ran up. It grabbed the whole bag! Athena said, "Oh no!" The squirrel ran to a big tree. The bag had a hole in it. Apples fell out of the bag. They were round. They rolled down the grass.

The apples rolled near a bench. A boy sat there with a toy truck. He stopped the apples with his truck. "Here you go," he said. Athena picked up her apples. She shared one with the boy. The ducks got more bread. "Thank you," Athena said. The boy pushed his truck again. Vroom!

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Abigail sat at the little red table. There was a tablet in front of her. It was dark and still. She wanted to draw a big round sun on it.

"Press the round button," said Miss Kim. Abigail pressed it. The screen lit up. She had made the dark screen turn bright. Miss Kim smiled and helped her tap the drawing app. It had a picture of a paint brush. Abigail tapped it, and the white page appeared. She drew a round sun. Then she drew a bird. She made the bird fly across the page with one long line.

Tommy came to the table next. He wanted a turn too. Abigail saw him waiting. She pressed the top button, and the screen went dark again. She put the tablet in the basket, just like Miss Kim showed. The tablet lay soft and quiet on top of a book.

"Your turn, Tommy," said Abigail. "Press the round button. Watch it light up." Tommy pressed it. The bright screen came back. "It works!" he said. Abigail went to the toy corner and picked up a round ball.

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
story:
Penelope wanted to wear her boots at daycare. But when she reached for her bag, one boot was gone.

"Where is my boot?" she asked. Her friend Tom looked under the table. "Not here," he said.

After snack time, they washed their hands. The water was warm. Penelope watched the bubbles slide down her fingers. Then she saw something stuck in the drying rack. It was her boot, full of soapy water!

"Yuck!" said Tom, and he laughed. "Your boot took a bath!"

Miss Anna poured the water out. She helped Penelope dry the boot with a towel. Penelope wiggled her toes inside. The boot was warm and damp.

At nap time, Penelope put the boot beside her mat. "Sleep now," she whispered.

When she woke up, the boot was dry. She pushed her foot in. It fit just right. Penelope stomped around the room. Stomp, stomp, stomp!

"My boots match again!" she said. Tom clapped, and they went to color a picture of two happy boots.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
It was Charlie's first day of school. She stood by the fence. Her tummy felt funny. She wanted a friend, but she did not know how.

A boy sat in the sandbox. He had a red truck. He poured sand into the truck. The sand made a little hill. Charlie watched and watched. She walked over slowly. She picked up a small cup. She scooped sand and poured it in too. Now the hill was bigger. The boy smiled at her.

Then they dug a long line in the sand. "Look, a worm road," said the boy. A real worm wiggled into the hole. It made the sand move. "Silly worm," said Charlie, and she laughed. The teacher rang the bell. Charlie and her new friend ran to the line, hand in hand.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Felix wanted to paint a picture for Grandma. He hoped she would love it. At school, there were paint cups on the table. There was red paint. There was blue paint. There was yellow paint. There was green paint.

Felix picked the red brush first. He made a big red sun. Then he dipped his brush in the blue cup. But the brush was still red. The blue cup turned purple!

"Oh no," said Felix. "My blue is gone!" He felt a little scared. Grandma loved blue. He wanted blue flowers in the picture.

Miss Mia came over. "Try a clean brush," she said. She gave him a fresh one. Felix dipped it in the blue cup. The blue stayed blue! He made five blue flowers.

Then he painted a green frog. He painted a yellow moon. He painted red spots on the frog, with a clean brush each time.

"Grandma will say wow," said Felix. He held the picture up high. The red sun smiled down on the blue flowers.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Ava sat in her car seat. She was hungry. "Mom, I want a snack," she said. "We will stop soon," said Mom. The car went past a big farm. Ava saw a cow. Then she saw a sheep. Then she saw a horse. "Animals!" said Ava. She waved at them.

The car stopped at a small shop. Mom held Ava's hand. They went inside. Ava saw apples, bread, and milk. "Those are foods," said Mom. Ava picked a red apple. Then she saw a bin of small cars. "Can I look at the toys?" she asked. "Just look," said Mom. Ava found a tiny blue car. It had kind eyes painted on it.

At the counter, Mom gave the man money. The man put the apple and the little car in a bag. "The car too?" asked Ava. Mom smiled. "The car too." In the car, Ava ate her apple. She held her new toy. The cow in the field watched them go by. Ava blinked, and the cow blinked back. "It saw me!" she said.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
story:
Gianna waited at the airport. She held a big paper sign. The sign said Grandma.

People came and went. One bag. Two bags. Three bags. Where was Grandma?

Then Gianna saw a red hat. "Grandma!" she yelled. Grandma hugged her tight. Grandma had one big suitcase. Gianna tried to pull it. It did not move. It was too heavy.

Grandma pushed the handle down. Then she pulled it up. The suitcase stood on little wheels. Now it rolled! "Can I fish for more wheels?" Gianna asked, looking around. She looked at a stroller. It had wheels too. Then a cart. Wheels again!

"Wheels make heavy things roll," Gianna said. Grandma laughed. "You are a smart girl. But one question first. Was that a mean old suitcase?" "No!" said Gianna. "It just needed wheels!"

Gianna rolled the suitcase all the way to the car. Wheel, wheel, wheel, it went.
